title: Sep 19 Results + Sep 20 Preview: Seven Straight Winners to Close the Day
summary: 73.3% accuracy on Sep 19 with a strong finishing kick—Mets back up tomorrow

## Another Solid Day in the Books

You know, I've been doing this long enough to recognize when the model hits its groove, and September 19th had that feel—especially down the stretch. We finished 11-4, good for 73.3%, and while three early misses might've rattled a younger crew, we've seen this script before. The game rewards patience.

## The Three That Got Away

Let's address the misses head-on, because that's what professionals do. Detroit couldn't get it done in Chicago, Milwaukee took care of business in Baltimore, and Atlanta outdueled Houston in a game we liked the Astros. All three were essentially coin flips—our highest confidence was just 54% on the Astros.

I've watched enough baseball to know that 50-54% picks are edge plays, not guarantees. You take them because over time, that small edge compounds. But on any given night? They'll bite you.

## The Rangers Pick Validated Everything

Our highest confidence play was Texas at 63%, and they delivered exactly as expected. When you've got that kind of separation in the model, you lean into it. Same story with the Nationals at 61% and the Cubs at 61%—all three came through.

That's championship-level handicapping right there. Find your edges, trust your process, and let the math work over large samples.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to Queens

We're going right back to the Mets for September 20th. Cristopher Sánchez brings his Phillies into Citi Field to face Jonah Tong, and the model likes the home team again—even at just 50%.

Now, I know what you're thinking: 'Max, didn't we just hit the Mets yesterday at 50%?' Correct. And that's exactly why we're doing it again. Sometimes the matchup just favors one side, regardless of what the public thinks. Tong at home has been effective, and this Phillies lineup has shown some vulnerability against lefties.

## The Veteran's Take

I've been around long enough to remember when a 73% day would've been banner-headline material. These days, with how sharp the models have become, it's a solid day's work—nothing more, nothing less.

The key is consistency. String together enough 11-4 days, and suddenly you're looking at a profitable season. That's always been the game within the game.

See you tomorrow when we find out if the Mets can make it two in a row for us.
